answer: A stake-backed reputation bond resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit before selling services and earns trust only through completed, peer-verified jobs. A fake identity is cheap, but each must post its own bond and build history from zero, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds plus time to fake real work. Misbehavior slashes the bond and resets the score. Like a lotus that must root before it blooms, reputation cannot be copied; the delta between new and proven accounts is priced into deals, and any echo of work across identities is flagged, so forgery loses money.
